notes.subject: Jenny Diersen email — 2027 vendor path
notes.body: On August 27, 2026, Jenny Diersen, South Salt Lake RDA Senior Program Manager, said the city was already full for both Celebrate South Salt Lake and Craftober Fest. She invited The Adventure Zone to complete the city's vendor form for 2027 opportunities and email-list inclusion: https://forms.gle/vfmR4b2GFodJ899KA. Desiree replied that the form would be completed next year. Contact: jdiersen@sslc.gov.

followUps.label: 2027 South Salt Lake vendor follow-up
followUps.reason: Complete Jenny Diersen's vendor form, confirm The Adventure Zone was added to the city opportunity list, and ask about 2027 Celebrate South Salt Lake and Craftober Fest needs.

notes.subject: Courtney email — reach out earlier for 2027
notes.body: On August 26, 2026, Courtney said the only large 2026 space was already booked for bouncy houses, but explicitly invited The Adventure Zone to reach out for a future year so pricing and fit could be reviewed. Desiree replied that we would contact them earlier for 2027. Contact: vendors.ecd@gmail.com.

followUps.label: 2027 Cowboy Days early outreach
followUps.reason: Courtney invited future-year contact and said the large space had already been assigned in 2026. Reconnect early enough to discuss space, pricing, and fit before another inflatable provider is booked.

notes.subject: Gaylord relationship and 2027 outreach path
notes.body: Gaylord is a prior Adventure Zone relationship. In 2026 the new Gaylord Association cancelled the Memorial Day event and considered moving it to Labor Day. Christina Mau later referred The Adventure Zone to Steve Lemonidis (slemonidis@vibeconcepts.com), but multiple 2026 outreach attempts received no response. On August 19 Christina said she was not planning the Labor Day event and believed it had barely been advertised. Preserve Christina as a helpful relationship contact (christina@saltaevents.com, 303-726-6054), but direct 2027 event outreach to Steve and the current Gaylord Association.

followUps.label: 2027 Gaylord event follow-up
followUps.reason: Prior client/relationship with a changed organizer and event timing. Contact Steve Lemonidis and the current Gaylord Association early to confirm whether a 2027 Memorial Day or Labor Day event is planned and whether Adventure Zone can return.

notes.subject: Jean Ray email — 2026 entertainment budget allocated
notes.body: On August 27, 2026, Jean Flynn Ray said Sheridan Celebrates' 2026 entertainment budget was already allocated. Desiree replied that The Adventure Zone would reach out earlier for 2027 before plans and budget were set. Current relationship contact: Jean Flynn Ray, jeanfray@gmail.com, 720-401-3417.

followUps.label: 2027 Sheridan Celebrates budget outreach
followUps.reason: Reach Jean before the 2027 entertainment plan and budget are allocated. Reference her 2026 reply and ask when proposals are reviewed.

notes.subject: Silverton Creative District email — future consideration
notes.body: On August 18, 2026, Silverton Creative District said the 2026 event was already set but would keep The Adventure Zone in mind for the future. Contact: info@silvertoncreativedistrict.org.

followUps.label: 2027 Silverton early outreach
followUps.reason: The organizer said they would keep Adventure Zone in mind for the future. Reconnect while 2027 entertainment and space decisions are still open.

notes.subject: Debbie Benson email — repeated footprint and free-kids-area conflict
notes.body: On August 18, 2026, vendor chair Debbie Benson said Adventure Zone had made the same request in prior years and the festival must pass: there is not enough footprint for inflatables and its kids area is intended to remain free/no-cost. Treat this as a recurring structural mismatch, not a timing issue. Do not schedule routine annual outreach unless the venue footprint or kids-area model changes. Contacts: debandlyle007@gmail.com and peter.sherman18@live.com.

notes.subject: Nicki Simon email — budget objection and commercial options
notes.body: On August 18, 2026, race director Nicki Simon said the Adventure Zone concept sounded fun but the WYO-131 budget was tight. This is a budget objection rather than a format rejection. For a future proposal, explain that under the right attendance, placement, and operating circumstances Adventure Zone may consider either (1) a pay-per-play/no-upfront structure with a percentage of ticket-box sales paid to the event, or (2) a guaranteed-pay structure in which public sales offset an agreed minimum. Any specific commercial offer still requires approval. Contact: wyo131gravel@landercycling.org; copied address wyo131gravel@gmail.com; phone 775-901-6917.

followUps.label: 2027 WYO-131 commercial follow-up
followUps.reason: Reconnect early with Nicki and explore whether the 2027 event's attendance, footprint, and operating setup could support an approved pay-per-play or guaranteed-pay arrangement despite the tight budget.

notes.subject: Volunteer Team email — event-format mismatch
notes.body: On August 18, 2026, the Timpanogos Storytelling Festival volunteer team said it is not that kind of festival. Treat this as a format mismatch rather than a lead needing annual follow-up. Contact used: volunteer@timpfest.org.

notes.subject: Kevin McHugh email — venue has no inflatable footprint
notes.body: On August 17, 2026, Kevin McHugh said Artfest has a kids zone but no room for inflatables because the event is confined to Perry Street and Festival Park and most space is occupied by artists and sponsor tents. Treat as a venue-footprint restriction, not a late-contact issue. Do not schedule routine annual outreach unless the site layout changes. Contact: kevin@castlerock.org; 303-520-4663 mobile; 303-688-4597 office.

notes.subject: Jamee Johnston email — Mini Zone interest with no final reply
notes.body: On August 13, 2026, Jamee Johnston asked whether The Adventure Zone had a smaller option because the main package appeared too large for Tomato Days. Adventure Zone replied with a scaled-down/Mini Zone example: obstacle course, 18-foot slide, Cute Bouncy House, Awesome Bounce House Combo, Fun Playland and Toxic Meltdown; $6,000 for up to four days; three to four carnival games charged directly to the public at $5–$8 per game; approximately 3,000–5,000 square feet. No reply was received after that proposal. Preserve this as a strong example for future limited-footprint leads, but verify current units, count, price, footprint and commercial approval before reusing it. Contact: Jamee Johnston, communityevents@hoopercity.gov, 801-732-1064 ext. 2.

followUps.label: 2027 Tomato Days Mini Zone follow-up
followUps.reason: Jamee showed interest and specifically asked for a smaller option, but the 2026 Mini Zone proposal received no final reply. Reconnect early for 2027, confirm available footprint, and present a currently approved scaled-down package.
